Name: guarded_l2s_merging
Title: Teaching Without Talking: Capability-Guarded Cross-Scale Merging of a Quantized Student Under a Synthetic-Data Ban
Short Hypothesis: When synthetic data is forbidden, classic sequence-level knowledge distillation is impossible, so the only cheap channel for a large model to 'train' a small model is weight space. We hypothesize that (i) a large same-family teacher can improve a small QAT student (gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-q4_0) purely through weight-space signals — teacher-Fisher importance masks computed with forward passes on real TMMLU+ text that guide TIES/DARE sparsification and MoE routing in MergeKit — outperforming unguided merging; and (ii) treating MMLU/GSM8K/IFEval non-regression as a hard feasibility constraint (rather than a post-hoc check) yields a Pareto frontier of merge configs where the best feasible config differs systematically from the unconstrained accuracy-maximizing one. This setting (quantized student + real-data-only + no-regression constraint) is the cleanest testbed for this question and cannot be answered by prior same-scale, unquantized, unconstrained merging studies.
Related Work: Yadav et al. (2024, 'What Matters for Model Merging at Scale') and Hitit et al. (2025, 'in-the-wild' merging) ran large systematic merging studies, but exclusively over same-scale, full-precision models and without capability-regression constraints; we differ in scale asymmetry (large→small), a QAT-quantized student, and a constrained-optimization framing. OptiMerge (2026) optimizes merge configurations evolutionarily but uses synthetic task evaluations without real-data-only constraints and no quantized models. MobileLLM-Pro (2025) combines specialist merging with 4-bit QAT, but relies on self-distillation (generated data) and does not study merge-method robustness on QAT weights. Token-scaled logit distillation (Kim et al., NeurIPS 2023) distills into QAT students but requires teacher logits on training text; our teacher never generates or scores text for training — it only produces importance masks. No prior work studies teacher-masked merging (using a large model's Fisher information to prune a small model's task vectors) nor Pareto-feasible merge selection under explicit benchmark non-regression.
Abstract: Model merging promises cheap capability transfer, but prior large-scale studies merge same-size, full-precision models and treat general-capability regression as an afterthought. We study a harder, practically motivated regime: a small quantization-aware-trained (QAT) student (gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized) must absorb localized knowledge from a larger same-family teacher using only real examination data (TMMLU+), with synthetic data strictly forbidden. The ban on synthetic data removes classic knowledge distillation from the toolbox, leaving weight space as the only large→small transfer channel. We therefore introduce teacher-masked merging: the large teacher computes per-parameter Fisher importance on real TMMLU+ text (forward passes only — the teacher never generates a token), and these masks guide task-vector trimming in TIES/DARE-TIES dense merges and expert/router construction in MergeKit MoE upcycling. We execute a fully logged, reproducible 48-configuration sweep (4 merge methods × 2 architectures {dense, MoE} × 3 guidance modes {none, magnitude, teacher-Fisher} × 2 densities), evaluating every candidate on TMMLU+ and, under a strict non-regression contract, on MMLU, GSM8K, and IFEval. We report the feasible Pareto frontier of merge configurations, test whether QAT students are disproportionately fragile to sparsification-based merging, and release all locked YAML configs, data hashes, and evaluation logs as a reusable MergeKit template. Our results provide the first evidence on whether large models can teach small quantized models without saying a word.
Experiments:
Phase 0 (Setup): Download ikala/tmmluplus into /data/ (train/val/test by official subject splits; decontaminate against MMLU). Baseline-evaluate gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized on TMMLU+, MMLU, GSM8K, IFEval via lm-evaluation-harness (pinned version, logged seeds).
Phase 1 (Expert pool): Fine-tune the E2B student on 4 disjoint TMMLU+ subject supergroups (real data only) + 1 all-data expert; fixed hyperparameters; 2 seeds.
Phase 2 (Teacher masks): A larger same-family teacher (gemma-4-E4B-it; fallback gemma-3-12b-it with shared tokenizer) computes per-layer Fisher importance via forward passes on TMMLU+ train text only. Masks are transferred to the student by relative layer index (both Gemma-family stacks), and used to (a) replace magnitude-based trimming in TIES/DARE-TIES (teacher-Fisher top-k) and (b) initialize/gate MoE router expert assignment.
Phase 3 (48-config sweep): 4 methods {linear, task-arithmetic, TIES, DARE-TIES} × 2 modes {dense, MergeKit MoE upcycling with 4 subject experts} × 3 guidance {unguided, magnitude-masked, teacher-Fisher-masked} × 2 densities {0.5, 0.7} = 48 locked MergeKit YAMLs, each with fixed seed, git commit, and data hash.
Phase 4 (Evaluation): Every candidate evaluated on TMMLU+ accuracy (primary), MMLU/GSM8K/IFEval (regression tolerance ≤0.5pp vs baseline). Metrics: TMMLU+ overall + per-subject accuracy, guardrail deltas, feasible Pareto frontier, bootstrap CIs for method comparisons.
Phase 5 (Analyses): (a) QAT-robustness: re-quantize merged bf16 models to q4_0 and measure degradation vs the QAT-native baseline; (b) λ scaling-coefficient sweep for the best method; (c) MoE router entropy vs per-subject accuracy correlation; (d) ablation of mask-transfer granularity (per-layer vs per-block).
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Cross-width teachers cannot be weight-merged directly into E2B; we mitigate by using the teacher only for Fisher-mask guidance (logit-free, generation-free) and by including a same-width control arm where the 'large' teacher is a weight-space ensemble of experts. 2) QAT checkpoints may be unstable under sparsification-based merging; we mitigate by merging in bf16 and reporting both bf16 and re-quantized q4_0 scores — if QAT fragility is confirmed, it is itself a novel negative result. 3) A 2B student has a capacity ceiling on TMMLU+; gains may be modest, but the feasible-frontier and no-regression findings transfer. 4) TMMLU+ subject-slice fine-tunes may overfit small slices; mitigated by early stopping on val and 2-seed replication. 5) Compute: ~48 × (1 GPU-hour merge + ~2 GPU-hours eval) ≈ 150–300 GPU-hours, feasible on a single academic A100/H100 node. 6) Fisher-mask transfer across depths assumes rough layer correspondence; the per-block ablation tests this assumption directly.

Name: null_expert_deferral
Title: The Null Expert: Can Merged MoEs Learn to Defer What They Don't Know?
Short Hypothesis: Capability regression in model merging is usually treated as an optimization problem (constrain the merge, then check benchmarks). We test a stronger, architectural hypothesis: if the frozen base model is included as an explicit routable 'null expert' inside a MergeKit-upcycled MoE, a router trained ONLY on real TMMLU+ text (no synthetic data, no OOD examples) will learn to route in-distribution exam inputs to subject experts while spontaneously deferring unfamiliar inputs (MMLU/GSM8K/IFEval) to the untouched base expert, yielding non-regression by construction rather than by constraint. A secondary hypothesis gives the mandated large-to-small channel a generation-free form: a larger same-family teacher 'teaches by curating' — forward-only confidence margins on real TMMLU+ examples weight the curricula used to fine-tune the small student's subject experts and router — outperforming uniform curation. The constrained testbed (QAT 2B student, real-data-only ban, hard non-regression rule) is the cleanest place to ask whether routing purity can replace merge regularization; no simpler setting isolates this mechanism.
Related Work: Our previous proposal (guarded_l2s_merging) used teacher-Fisher masks to guide sparsification and treated non-regression as a feasibility constraint; here the preservation mechanism is fundamentally different — emergent deferral routing to a frozen null expert — and the teacher channel is data curation rather than weight masks. Sparse upcycling (Komatsuzaki et al. 2023) and Branch-Train-Mix (Sukhbaatar et al. 2024) build MoEs from branched experts but include no base/null expert and study no OOD deferral; Branch-Train-Merge (Li et al. 2022) routes to separate full models at inference, not merged weights. MergeKit's frankenMoE initializes gates from prompt hidden states but no published work trains the router for OOD deferral or studies base-as-expert for capability preservation. MoLEM (Yu et al. 2026) and motion-language LoRA-MoE (Taetz et al. 2026) route to parameter-ADDITIVE modules with pretrained fallback in continual-learning agents; we route among weight-MERGED experts including the base itself, under a QAT student and real-data-only ban, with routing purity as a measured mechanism. MoE-compression work (MC-SMoE, Merging-Experts-into-One) goes the opposite direction. Data-selection work (LESS, DsDm, Sorscher et al.) uses model signals to pick training data but not a larger teacher curating real exam data for merged-expert specialization under a synthetic-data ban.
Abstract: Merged models forget: fine-tuned experts fused into one network trade away general capabilities for task gains, and current practice manages this trade-off with regularization and post-hoc benchmark checks. We ask whether forgetting can instead be prevented architecturally, by giving the merged model an explicit way to say 'not my department.' We introduce null-expert deferral merging: the frozen base model (gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized) is included as a routable expert in every MoE layer upcycled by MergeKit, alongside subject experts fine-tuned on disjoint TMMLU+ subject groups using only real data (synthetic data strictly forbidden). The router is trained on TMMLU+ text alone; we test whether it spontaneously defers out-of-distribution inputs to the frozen base, preserving MMLU, GSM8K, and IFEval by construction. The mandated large-to-small paradigm is realized without any model-generated tokens: a larger same-family teacher performs forward-only passes over real TMMLU+ examples and its confidence margins define curricula for expert and router training. We execute a fully logged, reproducible 48-configuration sweep (2 architectures {dense, MoE} x 4 merge methods {linear, task-arithmetic, TIES, DARE-TIES} x 3 base-participation modes {absent, static floor/component, adaptive null-expert deferral} x 2 curation modes {uniform, teacher-curated}), evaluating every candidate on TMMLU+, MMLU, GSM8K, and IFEval under a <=0.5pp regression contract. Beyond accuracy, we introduce routing-purity diagnostics — the fraction of benchmark tokens deferred to the null expert — and test whether deferral rate predicts capability preservation, offering a mechanistic, interpretable account of when merging forgets and how routing can prevent it.
Experiments:
Phase 0 (Setup): Download ikala/tmmluplus into /data/ (official splits; hash-logged; decontaminate vs MMLU). Baseline-evaluate the QAT student on TMMLU+, MMLU, GSM8K, IFEval with pinned lm-evaluation-harness and logged seeds.
Phase 1 (Teacher curation, large-to-small channel): A larger same-family teacher (gemma-4-E4B-it; fallback gemma-3-12b-it, shared tokenizer) makes forward-only passes over TMMLU+ train, scoring gold-option logprob margins per example (zero tokens generated). Examples are bucketed into {teacher-confident-correct, uncertain, teacher-wrong}; curation mode 'teacher' upweights confident-correct and orders easy-to-hard; mode 'uniform' is the control.
Phase 2 (Expert pool): Fine-tune the E2B student on 4 disjoint TMMLU+ subject supergroups (+1 all-data expert), real data only, fixed hyperparameters, 2 seeds, early stop on val.
Phase 3 (48-config sweep): 2 architectures {dense, MoE upcycling} x 4 methods {linear, task-arithmetic, TIES, DARE-TIES} x 3 base-participation modes {A: experts only; S: static base component (dense: lambda_base floor in {0.25}; MoE: base expert with fixed positive gate bias); N: adaptive null expert (MoE: base as routable expert-zero, gates fine-tuned on TMMLU+ with load-balancing loss, experts frozen; dense counterpart: per-layer lambda_base greedily selected on TMMLU+ val)} x 2 curation {uniform, teacher} = 48 locked MergeKit YAMLs, each with fixed seed, git commit, data hash.
Phase 4 (Evaluation): Every config evaluated on TMMLU+ (overall + per-subject accuracy) and MMLU/GSM8K/IFEval (regression tolerance <=0.5pp vs baseline). Metrics: feasible Pareto frontier (TMMLU+ vs worst guardrail delta), bootstrap CIs, and ROUTING PURITY: per-benchmark fraction of tokens routed to the null expert (hypothesis: high on MMLU/GSM8K/IFEval, low on TMMLU+ for mode N), subject-routing concentration vs per-subject gains, and correlation between deferral rate and capability delta across all MoE configs.
Phase 5 (Analyses): (a) QAT robustness: re-quantize merged bf16 to q4_0 and report degradation; (b) router-temperature sweep: does sharpening increase deferral purity without hurting TMMLU+?; (c) ablation: router trained with vs without load balancing; (d) best-config lambda/temperature replication on second seed.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The router may NOT learn spontaneous OOD deferral (softmax confidence on unfamiliar inputs could still favor subject experts); mode N would then collapse to mode S — but this is itself a clean, informative negative result, and routing-purity diagnostics explain why. 2) Dense-mode 'adaptive' is only per-layer static at inference, so the arch x mode interaction is partially asymmetric by design; we report it as a control, not the headline. 3) Null-expert MoE holds ~5 expert MLPs (~11GB bf16) — fits a single A100/H100; eval cost (~48 x 4 benchmarks, ~250-400 GPU-hours total) is the main budget. 4) GSM8K on a 2B QAT student has low absolute scores; deltas remain measurable and we report CIs. 5) Teacher-curation gains may be small if TMMLU+ train is already clean; the uniform arm isolates this. 6) Cross-width teacher cannot be weight-merged; used only for forward-only curation, consistent with the no-synthetic-data rule (margins are scores on real labels, not generated text). 7) QAT fragility under merging is mitigated by bf16 merging with re-quantization reporting.
